judgements.reason: Both are essentially already in the library and neither imports theory from another roadmap; Hodge's two summits (semisimplicity of polarizable structures in Semisimple.lean, Deligne strictness in Mixed/Strictness.lean) are proved and only the abelian-category packaging and a weight-one lattice constructor remain, whereas StandardDistributions still lacks one of its named families outright - the nonsingular Wishart density on the positive-definite cone, for which only the Gaussian-Gram law wishartGramMeasure exists.

StandardDistributions is built bar the nonsingular Wishart density, on top of Mathlib measure theory and TauCeti's symmetricLebesgue/Cholesky machinery; LocallyAnalyticDistributions must first create nonarchimedean functional analysis (locally convex, Frechet and LF spaces over K and their duals), then locally analytic function spaces, the unbounded Amice transform, admissible growth, affinoid character spaces (no Tate algebras exist in the baseline) and Fredholm/slope theory, plus the completed group rings and pseudo-measures of PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras.

LocallyAnalyticDistributions needs nonarchimedean functional analysis, the unbounded Amice transform, rigid character spaces and Fredholm/slope theory over about ten stacked layers, but GlobalQuadraticForms needs more: all of the Hilbert symbol, local classification and Witt ring from QuadraticFormInvariants (12 unbuilt layers) sitting on essentially all of class field theory - the Artin map, local and global reciprocity, the Hasse norm theorem and Hilbert reciprocity, of which the baseline has only class formations and low-degree continuous cohomology (11 unbuilt layers) - before its own seven unbuilt layers.

Both stack about ten substantial missing theories, but BelyiMaps must build three unrelated ones - Riemann surfaces with analytic Riemann existence (neither library has any Riemann surface theory), the algebraization bridge to algebraic curves with the Hurwitz formula, and profinite/pro-ell arithmetic culminating in the branch-cycle and pro-ell peripheral theorems and faithfulness - whereas GlobalQuadraticForms, though it needs the whole of class field theory and the local quadratic invariants, is a single connected line of classical algebraic number theory over a substrate (Witt cancellation, Witt extension, weak approximation, real signatures) that is already in place.

BelyiMaps is classical and self-contained: Riemann surfaces, Riemann existence, Belyi's theorem, Weil descent and pro-ell peripheral theory on top of covering-space theory and function-field curves that Tau Ceti already has. GlobalGaloisDeformations needs Galois cohomology of G_{F,S} with Poitou-Tate duality and dual Selmer groups, the complete-local coefficient category and Schlessinger representability, and local deformation rings whose p-adic Hodge conditions drag in adic spaces, perfectoid spaces and crystalline cohomology - 21 upstream roadmaps of which the baseline has none.

Both sit on Galois cohomology and Poitou-Tate duality that the baseline lacks entirely; GlobalGaloisDeformations adds deformation theory and local deformation rings with their p-adic Hodge conditions, while the cyclotomic main conjecture additionally requires the full Iwasawa apparatus (Lambda-modules with Weierstrass preparation and characteristic ideals, Coleman power series, Dirichlet p-adic L-functions, Ferrero-Washington) and the abstract Euler/Kolyvagin system machinery ES.0-ES.8 before Rubin's divisibility and equality, a slightly larger and more deeply stacked total.

ModularCurves is a very large but self-contained tower - relative Cartier divisors, elliptic curves over a base, Drinfeld structures, p-divisible groups and Serre-Tate, cyclicity and coarse moduli, with 37 of 58 stages unbuilt - and needs no other roadmap; the cyclotomic main conjecture stacks six unbuilt theories on one another (Iwasawa algebras and measures, Coleman power series, p-adic L-functions, Poitou-Tate and Selmer/Iwasawa cohomology, integral Iwasawa theory, abstract Euler and Kolyvagin systems) before its own five layers, which is a larger total and a deeper stack.

ModularCurves needs one book's worth of scheme-theoretic moduli built on Mathlib schemes and TauCeti Cartier duality; EllipticRegulators needs Deligne cohomology, the elliptic dilogarithm, and algebraic K-theory of schemes from nothing (there is no K-theory in either library), together with arithmetic modular curves and, for ER.7, the modularity theorem itself - which brings Galois deformations, patching and the GL_2 transfer tower with it.

EllipticRegulators imports the whole of GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer through the modularity theorem it needs for ER.7, and then adds Deligne cohomology, the Bloch-Wigner and elliptic dilogarithms, twelve K-theory and regulator roadmaps (K_2 with tame symbols, motivic and etale K-theory, syntomic regulators), CM Hecke characters and Deuring's theorem, and arithmetic modular curves with modular units.

Kato's Euler system needs the automorphic Galois representations attached to modular forms - hence most of GL_2 automorphic theory and the endoscopic transfer beneath it - and on top of that Siegel units, K_2 and syntomic regulators, arithmetic modular curves with moment maps, modular-symbol p-adic L-functions and the cyclotomic main-conjecture machinery, before explicit reciprocity and the divisibility.

P-adic differential equations needs Robba rings, the local monodromy theorem, rigid cohomology with finiteness and duality, and the l-adic Weil II apparatus beneath it - about 21 upstream roadmaps; KatoEulerSystems needs a strictly wider set (67 upstream roadmaps), including Siegel units and modular-curve geometry, all of K-theory and syntomic regulators, the automorphic Galois representation tower, Iwasawa theory and the cyclotomic main conjecture.

Both need the l-adic etale and perverse-sheaf foundation that the baseline entirely lacks, but Endoscopic adds endoscopic data and transfer factors, the Hitchin fibration and Ngo's support theorem for the fundamental lemma, the stable and twisted trace formulas, Shimura and Igusa varieties with trace formulas for correspondences, local Langlands for GL_m, and the Lubin-Tate/Drinfeld towers with their diamond-theoretic duality.

Excursion imports ET.0-ET.4 and ET.6/ET.6a - transfer factors, the fundamental lemma, the stabilized trace formula and the two-tower realization - for its GL_n comparison, and then needs the entire Fargues-Scholze geometrization on top: diamonds and v-stacks, the Fargues-Fontaine curve, Bun_G with Newton strata, lisse and solid sheaf categories, geometric Satake and Hecke stacks, and Langlands parameter stacks.

Excursion's Fargues-Scholze layer is the deeper single edifice, but GeneralizedHeegnerCycles needs a strictly larger total: it too imports the endoscopic transfer tower (through Gross-Zagier and GL_2), and adds Kuga-Sato geometry over arithmetic modular curves, algebraic cycles with etale and p-adic Abel-Jacobi maps, CM and ring class field theory, p-adic Hodge regulators and phi-Gamma modules, Iwasawa cohomology, Hida families and the anticyclotomic p-adic L-function.

The two share modular-curve geometry, p-adic Hodge regulators, Iwasawa cohomology and the Euler/Kolyvagin machinery; GeneralizedHeegnerCycles additionally needs Kuga-Sato varieties with their coefficient projectors and higher-dimensional cycles with Abel-Jacobi maps, CM points and ring class fields via HeegnerPointEulerSystems and Gross-Zagier (which imports the modularity and Shimura-curve chain), and Hida families with Yager modules - where Kato needs only Siegel units and K_2 regulators on the curve itself.

LocallyAnalyticDistributions must build nonarchimedean functional analysis, the unbounded Amice transform, affinoid character spaces and Fredholm/slope theory on top of Mathlib's Mahler basis and bounded p-adic measures, which already exist; BelyiMaps has more layers still missing and they stack further - triangle groups and van Kampen, Riemann surfaces and analytic Riemann existence, algebraization with the Hurwitz formula, Belyi's theorem, Weil descent, profinite pi_1 with the branch-cycle theorem, and the pro-ell peripheral theorem with faithfulness.

GeneralizedHeegnerCycles imports the endoscopic transfer tower itself (via Gross-Zagier and GL_2 automorphic theory) and then adds Kuga-Sato geometry, algebraic cycles and Abel-Jacobi realizations, CM and ring class field theory, p-adic Hodge regulators, Selmer and Iwasawa cohomology, Hida families and the anticyclotomic p-adic L-function with its nonvanishing theorem.

Excursion needs the Fargues-Scholze package (diamonds, Bun_G, geometric Satake, parameter stacks) plus ET.6/ET.6a, which is the deepest single tower here; EllipticRegulators needs a larger total - the whole of algebraic and motivic K-theory with regulators and polylogarithms (absent from both libraries), complex uniformisation and Deligne cohomology, CM Hecke characters, arithmetic modular curves with modular units, syntomic regulators, and the modularity theorem with the deformation-theoretic and automorphic machinery beneath it.

GlobalGaloisDeformations needs Galois cohomology with Poitou-Tate, deformation functors and local deformation rings with p-adic Hodge conditions; GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer needs the entire smooth-representation and automorphic apparatus (GL_2 of the adeles, Whittaker models, L- and epsilon-factors, the converse theorem, the trace formula) plus local Langlands for GL_m from EndoscopicTransfer ET.6, and therefore transfer factors and the fundamental lemma, before Jacquet-Langlands, base change and Langlands-Tunnell.

The cyclotomic main conjecture stacks Iwasawa algebras, Coleman power series, p-adic L-functions, Selmer/Iwasawa cohomology and Euler/Kolyvagin systems - but Mathlib already supplies Mahler bases, bounded p-adic measures and much of the commutative algebra; the rigid-cohomology roadmap must build Robba rings and dagger algebras from nothing, prove the p-adic local monodromy theorem and Kedlaya's finiteness, duality and p-adic Weil II, and it sits on adic spaces, crystalline cohomology and the whole l-adic perverse/Weil II apparatus, none of which exists in the baseline.

GlobalQuadraticForms needs class field theory, the local quadratic invariants and Hasse-Minkowski - large but classical, and its field-generic substrate (Witt cancellation and extension, weak approximation, signatures) is in place; ModularCurves needs the entire scheme-theoretic theory of elliptic curves over a base - relative Cartier divisors, the scheme group law, Cartier-Nishi duality and the Weil pairing, Drinfeld level structures, the Katz-Mazur moduli formalism, p-divisible groups and Serre-Tate, cyclicity, coarse moduli and compactification - with 37 of its 58 stages unbuilt.

BelyiMaps needs Riemann surfaces, algebraization, Belyi's theorem and pro-ell peripheral theory on top of covering-space theory and function-field curves that Tau Ceti largely has; KatoEulerSystems needs Siegel units on arithmetic modular curves as schemes, K_2 and syntomic regulators (no K-theory exists in either library), the automorphic Galois representation and transfer tower, Iwasawa theory and the cyclotomic main conjecture, before explicit reciprocity.

Both need the modularity and GL_2 transfer chain and arithmetic modular curves; GeneralizedHeegnerCycles adds Kuga-Sato cycles, Hida families and anticyclotomic Iwasawa theory, while EllipticRegulators adds the larger block of algebraic, motivic and etale K-theory with Chern classes and syntomic regulators, polylogarithms and Borel regulators, complex uniformisation with Deligne cohomology, and CM Hecke characters with Deuring's comparison - a wider set of unbuilt subjects.

The cyclotomic main conjecture needs Iwasawa theory, Coleman power series, Selmer cohomology and Euler/Kolyvagin systems, with Mathlib's Mahler and measure theory already underneath; Endoscopic needs endoscopic data and transfer factors, perverse sheaves and the Hitchin fibration for the fundamental lemma, the stable and twisted trace formulas, Shimura and Igusa varieties, local Langlands for GL_m and the Lubin-Tate/Drinfeld towers - none of whose foundations (etale cohomology, reductive group harmonic analysis, diamonds) exist in the baseline.

LocallyAnalyticDistributions builds p-adic functional analysis, the unbounded Amice transform, character spaces and Fredholm theory over one prerequisite roadmap whose bounded-measure core is already in Mathlib; GlobalGaloisDeformations needs Galois cohomology of G_{F,S} with Poitou-Tate duality and dual Selmer groups, the complete-local coefficient category and representability, Taylor-Wiles primes, and local deformation rings whose p-adic Hodge conditions require adic spaces, perfectoid spaces and crystalline cohomology.
